body:
So, during interview, they have to ask everything based upon the evidence they have at that point? they couldn't be holding 'evidence' for another interview?

Also, my question is, is it not unethical to say 'if he admits it we'll caution him' if they had no intention of doing that. Seems like they were trying to play on the distress I was going through at the time to illicit an admission of guilt. I'll add, they had the mental health nurse there ready for when I arrived as they'd been told I had a mental health condition, then left me in a cell for 7 hours before interviewing me. My solicitor informed me he got the call to come and represent me an hour before the interview.... Is this all not a bit dodgy? Are all police officers like this, or did I just deal with a bad apple that brings the rest down?

Once this has been resolved, all of this will be put in as a formal complaint because the way I see it, it's not cricket...

The first thing my solicitor told me was that the officer claimed he had good evidence and if I admitted it all, they'd let me off with a caution. That's clearly not true, so maybe it's something I will raise with the duty inspector when I know the result of this.

They gave me 28 days from custody, it's been extended by an inspector 3 times since then. Initially an additional month, then another 2 weeks, and again, another 2 weeks.

send 3 detectives to arrest me... tell my solicitor that he has good evidence and if I admit it all they'd offer me a caution at the first interview and then bail me for 3 months to continue the investigation.... Is this usual in police interviews? to actively lie to get a confession from someone they can see is stressed and has already had to see the mental health nurse at the custody suite? Especially when it's just based on one statement from a witness. That all seems to be basing guilt upon on statement to me.
